correctness.rationale: Structural proof: order-3 automorphism descends to PGL2(F3), conjugate to x↦x+1; its geometric fixed infinity cannot be a reduced six-point branch of invariant degree six. Invariants under translation are F3[x³−x], so models y²=c((x³−x)²+a(x³−x)+b) with c∈{1,2}, a²−b nonzero; a↔−a yields eight arithmetic models. Independently enumerated all 3^7−1=2186 nonzero binary sextic coefficients; derivative gcd plus infinity-degree test leaves exactly 1296 geometrically squarefree forms. Independent 24-element PGL2(F3) action partitions into 69 orbits; exact F3/F9 point counts yield 50 Weil coefficient pairs. Exactly the eight stated target pairs have singleton orbit fibers, with orbit sizes [1,1,4,4,8,8,8,8]; no extrapolation from incomplete enumeration. Frobenius coefficient A1=#C(F3)−4 and A2=(#C(F9)−10+A1²)/2 checked. The supplied artifacts/verify.py was read as evidence; independent implementation produced same counts.
residual_risks: Equality of Weil polynomial identifies unpolarized Jacobian isogeny class, not generally curve isomorphism; uniqueness asserted only in these eight finite-field fibers.
Binary sextic orbit method uses complete squarefree invariant classification and F3-specific scalar action; no other fields covered.

value.rationale: Weil polynomial usually determines an unpolarized Jacobian isogeny class rather than a unique genus-two curve. The eight F3 symmetry isogeny classes unexpectedly isolate a single curve each, so a natural arithmetic invariant exactly detects a wild automorphism on a complete field-specific locus. This is a motivated exact finite classification, not an arbitrary list of eight coefficients.
residual_risks: Only F3 and rational automorphism; no statement about geometric automorphisms or other finite fields.
